subject: Interim update — control-plane scheduling imbalance affecting p95 and partial timeouts
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Spencer <maya.spencer@cardinalai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>; Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: Interim update — control-plane scheduling imbalance affecting p95 and partial timeouts

Hi Maya / CardinalAI team,

Thanks for the patience this morning. I wanted to provide a concise interim update while we complete the deeper RCA and postmortem.

What happened (brief):
- Between ~08:40–09:20 UTC we observed an increase in p95 and a small number of model timeouts for hosted text-generation requests routed to the multi-tenant control plane.
- Symptoms: elevated p95 (2–3x typical), sporadic 504/timeout responses for long-context requests, and higher cold-start rate on a subset of frontend workers.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- We throttled low-priority background traffic and rerouted heavy request paths to a warmed pool of dedicated inference workers.
- Rolled a targeted control-plane scheduler patch to reduce unfair backlog buildup (hotfix id: REDW-FIX-4921).

Customer impact:
- CardinalAI: observed ~7% of requests at peak experiencing higher-than-normal latency; <1% returned timeouts. We prioritized your production cluster for reroute and warming.

What we’re doing next:
- Full RCA underway (engineers are collecting scheduler traces, heap profiles, and queue metrics).
- Postmortem and remediation plan targeted by EOD Friday (local). We’ll publish the postmortem link and provide a scoped timeline for long-term fixes (control-plane backpressure controls and additional pre-warming heuristics).

Attachments: I’ve attached an interim timeline CSV and a heap excerpt we captured while reproducing the behavior locally.

If you need an immediate phone bridge, I’m available and can loop in our SRE lead.

Apologies for the disruption — we know latency is critical and we’re treating this with priority.

–Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 7 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Interim update — control-plane scheduling imbalance affecting p95 and partial timeouts

Internal notes / short RCA snapshot:
- Root cause (prelim): a regression in the control-plane scheduler introduced by a recent change to the token-bucketing heuristic. Under a specific request length distribution we observed unbounded backlog accumulation on ~12% of request shards, which caused worker starvation and increased cold-starts as routing attempted to shift load.
- Trigger: a change merged 2028-06-05 (PR #9187) that optimized per-tenant tokens-per-second accounting but inadvertently allowed bursts to bypass the intended smoothing window.

Mitigations performed:
- Hotfix: reverted the smoothing-window change (control_plane_patch.diff attached) and enforced a hard cap in the scheduler branch to limit backlog per-shard.
- Routing: temporarily prefer warmed-dedicated pools for customers flagged for SLO-critical traffic (CardinalAI included).

Next steps / timeline:
- Complete trace-level verification and run canary across 3 zones by 2028-06-08 18:00 UTC.
- Postmortem draft by 2028-06-09 EOD; final postmortem and follow-up checklist by 2028-06-12.

Will add quantitative test results to the postmortem and share the remediation tickets.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Platform Reliability

Subject: Re: Interim update — control-plane scheduling imbalance affecting p95 and partial timeouts

Hi Maya / David,

Short answers to your asks:
1) No user data was lost. The timeouts were at the request/response layer — we didn’t observe any persisted state inconsistencies or dropped customer data.
2) Recommended temporary client settings: increase client retry backoff to jittered 250–750ms and set request timeout to 30s for long-context calls. We’ll publish an engineer guidance note in the link below.

Status now: visible p95 and timeout rates have returned to near-baseline after the hotfix and the temporary routing change. We continue to monitor and will run the canary across two additional zones later today.

Public status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-06-07-scheduler-imbalance
Postmortem draft (internal link): https://drive.redwood.ai/incident-20280607/postmortem-draft

If you want a quick sync, we can do a 20-minute call at 15:00 UTC today.

Thanks again for the patience.

–Tessa
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 9 Jun 2028 16:40:00 -0000
Subject: Postmortem draft — control-plane scheduling imbalance (summary)

Maya / CardinalAI team,

Attached is the postmortem draft (link above). Below is an executive summary and the immediate remediation plan we’ll execute this week.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2028-06-07 08:40–09:25 UTC (root-cause exposure window).
- Impact: temporary latency spikes (p95 up to 3x) and ~0.8% request timeouts for a subset of long-context generation traffic. No persisted data loss.
- Root cause: regression in token-bucketing smoothing window resulting in backlog accumulation under specific request length distributions; scheduler allowed burst bypassing smoothing window (PR #9187).

Remediation plan (short-term):
- 1) Permanent revert of risky change and stricter unit tests around smoothing-window semantics (owner: Platform infra, ETA: 2028-06-12).
- 2) Add a per-shard hard backlog cap and alarm (owner: Scheduler team, ETA: 2028-06-09).
- 3) Improve canary coverage for request-length distributions in pre-prod (owner: QA, ETA: 2028-06-19).

Compensation / customer care:
- We recognize CardinalAI saw elevated latencies during a production run this morning. We will follow up with an offer to extend your committed Dedicated warm pool for two weeks at no charge while we complete the remediation and prove stability. Our account lead will follow up on contractual details.

If you have questions or want different remediation priorities, please let us know. We’ll finalize the postmortem and publish the public version on the status page by 2028-06-12.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Platform Reliability
